messages:
samira: quick heads-up — after the overnight optimizer rollout we're seeing a divergent signal: hosted canary p95 up ~3x in eu-west but only on requests that hit the new feature-flagged codepath. Dedicated premium pools showing milder effects. No customer 5xxs yet but degradation for a subset.

omar: which cohort exactly? feature-flagged requests across all regions or just eu-west?

samira: it's feature-flagged requests only. eu-west is worst (p95 ~420ms). Traffic slice for flagged users ~6%. deploy-bot also queued an autorevert for the flagged route.

deploy-bot: ALERT: flagged-route p95 breach (p95 > 300ms). Suggested actions: 1) autorevert flagged-route -> previous build (confidence 0.60) OR 2) partial rollback of flagged traffic only. Autorevert scheduled in 90s unless suppressed. Reason: feature-path allocator + cache churn.

ops-lee: suppress autorevert for 2m — we need traces across the feature boundary before nuking the signal. If we autorevert the whole build we lose the ability to diagnose.

samira: agree. We'll put an operator hold and capture spans + kv snapshots. Also propose a targeted rollback strategy: move flagged traffic off the new variant via traffic-slice routing (keep main rollout going). That reduces customer impact while preserving rollout progress.

cs-ravi: if we split routing, CS needs a list of affected accounts (flagged users) so we can proactively notify high-touch customers. Prep a short blurb dependent on the action we take.

ops-lee: capturing traces: `rdwctl collect --scope flagged-route --kinds traces,kv-stats --window 10m --out s3://rdw-dumps/1805556666-flagged-snap.tar.gz`  started. ETA ~80s.

samira: implementing operator hold and pin for flagged route: `releases pin --route flagged-feature --to v6.3.1 --reason "p95 spike; preserve traces"`  pin applied. Note: this only pauses progressive increase of flagged traffic; main rollout remains unaffected.

deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert suppressed by operator hold (actor: ops-lee). To re-enable: `deploybot enable-autorevert --route flagged-feature`

omar: proposal for rollback-exec: if traces point to allocator/mem-copy, do a targeted revert of the feature-flagged variant by changing traffic routing: `routing set --route flagged-feature --variant previous --scope hosted,dedicated:non-premium`  this removes flagged traffic from new codepath without touching the base image. For premium Dedicated pools, consider hotpatch first.

legal-karin: if we make a Dedicated-only change or partial rollback, we should log the customer-facing language and keep legal in the loop for any maintenance window notification. CS please cc legal on any account-specific outreach.

ops-lee: snapshot uploaded to s3://rdw-dumps/1805556666-flagged-snap.tar.gz. Flamegraphs show a sharp memcpy spike on the feature codec path and increased kv invalidations for keys prefixed by `ff/`. Looks like the feature changes cache key shape and causes repeated cold misses.

samira: decision then: perform routing-based rollback for flagged traffic (hosted + non-premium dedicated) -> route back to previous variant; for premium Dedicated pools, attempt hotpatch to preserve SLA while we test root cause. Will keep autorevert suppressed to avoid thrash.

deploy-bot: ACTION: executing routing update for flagged-route (hosted + dedicated:non-premium). Command: `routing set --route flagged-feature --variant v6.2.9 --scope hosted,dedicated:non-premium --reason "mitigate latency spike; preserve rollout"`  executing now.

deploy-bot: DONE: flagged-route routing adjusted. Estimated impacted traffic moved off new variant ~5.9% -> 0.4%.

ops-lee: applying hotpatch to premium dedicated pools: `opsctl patch config --unset feature_cache_key_v2 --pools premium-eu --reason "mitigate flagged-route kv churn"` then `rolling-restart --pools premium-eu --wait 45s`  running...

ops-lee: patch applied and restarts completed for premium-eu.

deploy-bot: MONITOR: within 4m of routing rollback + hotpatch, flagged-route p95 dropped eu-west 420ms -> 130ms and kv-miss rate normalized. Autorevert remains suppressed.

cs-ravi: notifying account teams for any premium customers who may have seen slight latency. Draft posted: "We routed flagged traffic away from a newly rolled out feature due to internal latency signals and applied a targeted fix to premium pools. No customer-facing errors observed; targeted customers may see short-lived improvements." Legal looped in.

samira: runbook for full rollback if metrics re-worsen: 1) create rollback ticket ops-RB-<ts> 2) pin global rollout and stop further promotions 3) run `releases rollback --to v6.2.9 --scope all` 4) monitor p95 and error-rate for 60m 5) publish postmortem.

omar: leaving autorevert suppressed for 45m to prevent flip-flop. We'll monitor dashboards and synthetic tests. If any region crosses p95 > 300ms again for >10m, escalate to full rollback per runbook.

ops-lee: I'll keep a watch on canary and flagged-route panels for the next hour and will alert on spikes. Ticket ops-RB-1805556666 created as precaution.

samira: postmortem owner assigned: @omar. Draft due EOD. Also add a short blurb to release notes: "Feature-flagged route temporarily rerouted to previous variant due to cache key change causing kv churn; targeted hotpatch applied to premium dedicated pools; rollout otherwise continues."

deploy-bot: INFO: rollout state: main rollout active; flagged-route traffic rolled back to v6.2.9 for scoped cohorts; autorevert suppressed for flagged-route.

cs-ravi: thanks all — will follow up with any customer replies. Closing thread after postmortem link is posted.
